state.seed_assertion: A common mistake in troubleshooting intermittent faults is panicking and abandoning systematic approaches in favor of quick fixes.

sentences.1: A common mistake in troubleshooting intermittent faults is panicking and abandoning systematic approaches in favor of quick fixes.
sentences.2: They sometimes panic and give up before actually trying to find the fault.
sentences.3: Or, in an effort to fix something quickly, they take the shotgun approach and miss some obvious things that a more systematic approach would uncover.
sentences.4: Quick diagnosis approach is appropriate for clearly defined faults where fast troubleshooting is the priority.
sentences.5: This paper proposes a novel data preprocessing method that converts numeric data into representative graphs (polygons) expressing all of the relationships between data variables in a systematic way based on Hamiltonian cycles.
sentences.6: A quick fix never enters the system.
sentences.7: Failing to document troubleshooting steps and results can cause engineers to repeat failed approaches and lose structure in their fault-finding process.
sentences.8: After a while, the engineer may start going in circles, applying fixes that have already been tried and rejected.
sentences.9: Measuring voltage at the source and return path is part of systematic troubleshooting to determine circuit condition.
sentences.10: These appear randomly, making systematic testing difficult.
sentences.11: If it is a single-unit fault that will not repeat, keeping the unit in quarantine until additional units show issues or until it is believed that it is a single unit issue (such as ESD to an exposed PCB) can be an acceptable approach.
sentences.12: Methodical questioning and data gathering before making changes is more effective for solving PLC problems than speed-based trial and error approaches.
